_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401909305.text: Charlotte have lost 9 of 10 and blew an 18-point lead to the Lakers. Charles Lee is taking criticism for sitting Brandon Miller and Coby White in overtime because of their minutes limits. At 0-2 in the Cup, Lee calls this one 'doubly important'. Atlanta have won 6 of 8 in November, including a first-ever home loss handed to OKC, and play their first home game since Nov 9. The angle leans towards Atlanta.

401909306.text: After the 30-point home loss to Chicago, Jordi Fernandez spoke of 'selfishness, finger-pointing' and said his message isn't getting through. Julius Randle called the loss 'embarrassing'. Moritz Wagner faces his former team, and his brother Franz, for the first time, a small emotional plus for Brooklyn. Overall the angle leans towards Orlando.

401909307.text: Both teams are 1-1 in Cup group play, so the stakes are real for both. Cleveland lost to Memphis after Sam Merrill missed two late free throws ('I feel like I cost the team the game'), and Kenny Atkinson has used nine starting lineups in 16 games. Indiana are still without Tyrese Haliburton, and Thomas Bryant faces his old team. The angle is close to neutral and leans slightly to Cleveland at home.

401909308.text: Toronto have lost six straight, most recently at Washington, and Darko Rajakovic's late-game plans are under scrutiny after three blown leads. Kawhi Leonard is still out with knee swelling, and the Raptors are 3-9 without him. Scottie Barnes is expected back. Detroit have won 4 of 5 by committee, and Cade Cunningham is probable after one game off. The angle leans clearly towards Detroit.

401909309.text: Both sides come in lifted. Washington ended an eight-game skid behind AJ Dybantsa's first double-double, and Chicago made a franchise-record 15 first-half threes in a 30-point rout in Brooklyn. Washington won the October meeting 124-120. The Bulls are without rookie Caleb Wilson (hand). No clear lean; neutral.

401909310.text: New Orleans are in turmoil. Dejounte Murray has requested a trade and posted, then deleted, a 'SABOTAGE' tweet. Zion Williamson called a blowout 'unacceptable', and first-year coach Jamahl Mosley drew an F grade after the loss to a short-handed Detroit. Trey Murphy III may return. OKC have lost 4 of 5 and are without Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren, and Gilgeous-Alexander calls it 'a new challenge'. The angle leans mildly towards OKC.

401909311.text: Utah ended a 12-game skid and then won at the Lakers, snapping LA's nine-game streak, despite losing Lauri Markkanen for at least a month. Will Hardy credited the team's intensity. They are still trying to end a seven-game home losing streak. Phoenix come off a comfortable win in Sacramento with no reported drama. The angle is close to neutral and leans slightly to Utah.

401909312.text: Alperen Sengun is questionable after being poked in both eyes on Nov 18, with a scratched cornea. Clint Capela is day-to-day, so Houston's frontcourt against Jokic is thin. Denver come in confident after rallying from 17 down to beat Boston, their fifth win in seven, and want to answer the 110-100 loss in Houston. The angle leans towards Denver, especially if Sengun sits.

401909313.text: Sacramento finished the worst homestand in franchise history (0-7), and Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis had a visible on-court exchange. Doug Christie is in the final secured year of his contract, with replacements already being floated. The Lakers, without Austin Reaves, are stung by losing to Utah, and Luka Doncic called his own game 'unacceptable'. The angle leans towards the Lakers.

401910023.text: Milwaukee have lost 12 straight, the worst 16-game start in franchise history. Taylor Jenkins has admitted 'what we're doing right now is not working', and the NBA's investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract hangs over the club. Philadelphia are rested after two days off and won in Orlando without Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey. The angle leans towards Philadelphia.

401910024.text: Portland come off an emotional night in Milwaukee, where Damian Lillard scored 33 on his return. They play again with no rest day, near the end of the road trip, without Deni Avdija (foot, possible return) and Ja Morant (hamstring). The defending champion Knicks have won three straight. Mike Brown is publicly backing the slumping Mikal Bridges as a starter. The angle leans slightly towards New York.

401910025.text: The Clippers have lost two straight, to Utah and San Antonio, are 0-5 on the road and are without Bradley Beal and Brandon Ingram. Dallas are 6-2 at home. Kyrie Irving is back after 19 months out, and Dusty May calls Cooper Flagg one of the league's fastest-rising stars. The angle leans towards Dallas.

401910026.text: Memphis have won five straight and go for a ninth straight road win, but the injury list is growing. Ty Jerome (hip) and Zach Edey (ankle) are out, and Jerami Grant left Thursday's game with a calf injury. Minnesota are 8-3 since Anthony Edwards' knee surgery, with Ayo Dosunmu and Jaden McDaniels stepping up, though they lost a close one at home to the Knicks. Close to neutral, leaning slightly to Minnesota at home.

401910027.text: New Orleans play the second night of a back-to-back amid a trade request from Dejounte Murray, Zion Williamson's public 'look in the mirror' challenge and heavy criticism of coach Jamahl Mosley. San Antonio are without Dylan Harper (hip, 1-3 weeks) but are 13-3. The angle leans towards San Antonio.

401910028.text: Boston blew a 17-point lead in Denver for their first back-to-back losses since March. Jayson Tatum's technical helped seal it ('That's on me'), so there is a response motive. Sacramento play the second night of a back-to-back after the worst homestand in franchise history, with Sabonis unhappy and coach Doug Christie under pressure. The angle leans towards Boston.
